extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges and Federally-facilitated Exchanges (FFEs), QHP issuers, CMS/HHS program staff, and Exchange program integrity reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and verification/audit requirements for Health Insurance Exchanges concerning APTC eligibility, verification, provider access, Essential Community Provider (ECP) rules, special enrollment period verification, and the State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of FTR policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must apply any such policy uniformly to all tax filers (and their spouses, if married).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan year 2028 requirement for 1-tax year FTR policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan year 2028 and beyond, an Exchange must implement a 1-tax year FTR policy described in paragraph (f)(4)(ii)(A) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — failed to file and reconcile for 1 tax year
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax filer and their spouse, if the tax filer is married, is considered to have failed to file and reconcile for 1 tax year if HHS notifies the Exchange ... that APTC payments were made on behalf of either the tax filer or the tax filer's spouse ... for the most recent year for which tax data would be utilized ... and the tax filer or the tax filer's spouse did not comply with the requirement to file an income tax return for that year ... and reconcile APTC for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References statutory filing requirements at 26 U.S.C. 6011, 6012 and implementing regulations in 26 CFR chapter I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — failed to file and reconcile for 2 tax years
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax filer and their spouse, if the tax filer is married, is considered to have failed to file and reconcile for 2 tax years if HHS notifies the Exchange ... that APTC payments were made ... for the 2 most recent consecutive tax years ... and the tax filer or the tax filer's spouse did not comply with the requirement to file an income tax return for those years ... and reconcile APTC for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References statutory filing requirements at 26 U.S.C. 6011, 6012 and 26 CFR chapter I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for Exchanges implementing 2-tax year FTR policy — 1-year failure notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Exchange implements a 2-tax year FTR policy, for tax filers failing to file and reconcile for 1 tax year the Exchange must either: (i) send a notification to the tax filer, consistent with the standards applicable to the protection of Federal Tax Information, informing the tax filer that the Exchange has determined they have failed to file and reconcile, and educate them of the need to file and reconcile or risk ineligibility if they fail a second year; or (ii) send a notification to either the tax filer or their enrollee informing them they may be at risk of being determined ineligible for APTC in the future, educating them on the requirement while not directly stating that the IRS indicates failure to file and reconcile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two alternative notice methods allowed: direct (explicit) or indirect (risk warning that avoids directly attributing the IRS finding). Notices must protect Federal Tax Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for Exchanges implementing 2-tax year FTR policy — 2-year failure notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Exchange implements a 2-tax year FTR policy, for tax filers failing to file and reconcile for 2 consecutive tax years the Exchange must either: (i) send a direct notification to the tax filer, consistent with FTI protection standards, that explicitly informs them the Exchange has determined they failed to file Federal income taxes and reconcile APTC and educate them of the need to file and reconcile or risk being determined ineligible for APTC after 2 consecutive tax years; or (ii) send an indirect notification to either the tax filer or their enrollee informing them they may be at risk of being determined ineligible after 2 consecutive tax years, educating them on the requirement while not directly stating the IRS indicates failure to file and reconcile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct notification must explicitly state determination; indirect notification must avoid directly attributing to IRS while still educating on filing/reconciliation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for Exchanges implementing 1-tax year FTR policy
rubrics_metrics.description: An Exchange that implements 1-tax year FTR policy must either: (1) send a notification to the tax filer, consistent with FTI standards, that informs the tax filer that the Exchange has determined they have failed to file and reconcile and of the need to file and reconcile and of the risk of being determined ineligible for APTC if they fail to file and reconcile immediately; or (2) send a notification to either the tax filer or their enrollee informing them they may be at risk of being determined ineligible for APTC in the future, educating on the requirement while not directly stating that the IRS indicates failure to file and reconcile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct vs indirect notice options; direct notice emphasizes immediate risk of ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification income discrepancy threshold (reasonable threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant's attestation to projected annual household income would qualify the taxpayer as an applicable taxpayer under 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b) and is more than a reasonable threshold above the annual household income computed using data sources, and the data indicates projected income is under 100% FPL and the Exchange has not verified MAGI-based income as within Medicaid/CHIP standard, the Exchange must proceed in accordance with §155.315(f)(1)–(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasonable threshold is established by the Exchange in guidance and approved by HHS, but must not be less than 10 percent, and can include a threshold dollar amount. The same reasonable threshold applies in related paragraph (c)(3)(vi)(C)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Household Income
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (c)(3), 'household income' means household income as specified in 26 CFR 1.36B-1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Family Size
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (c)(3), 'family size' means family size as specified in 26 CFR 1.36B-1(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of eligible noncitizen status via DHS SAVE
rubrics_metrics.description: For an applicant who has information or documentation of immigration status that can be verified through DHS's SAVE program and who attests to having an eligible noncitizen status as defined at §155.20, the Exchange must transmit information or documents to DHS for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Exchange cannot verify such attestation through DHS, it must follow procedures in §155.315(f)(1)–(4). The 'date on which the notice is received' means 5 days after the date on the notice unless applicant demonstrates otherwise. If still unable to verify at the conclusion of the period, the Exchange must determine the applicant ineligible for APTC and CSR, notify per §155.310(g), and discontinue payments per §155.330(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to require documentary evidence for SEP eligibility after termination
rubrics_metrics.description: At the option of the Exchange, the qualified individual provides satisfactory documentary evidence to verify his or her eligibility for an insurance affordability program or enrollment in a QHP through the Exchange following termination of Exchange enrollment due to a failure to verify such status within the time period specified in §155.315.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment verification requirement for Special Enrollment Periods (Federal platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 1, 2027, Exchanges on the Federal platform must conduct pre-enrollment verification of new applicants' eligibility for special enrollment periods. An Exchange meets this requirement if it verifies eligibility each plan year for the number of individuals newly enrolling through SEPs that equals at least 75 percent of all special enrollments based on prior year enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to verify eligibility for individuals for which verification is required, those individuals are not eligible for enrollment through that SEP. Individuals retain the right to appeal the eligibility determination under §155.505(b)(1)(iii). Exchanges may request modification per §155.315(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption eligibility — projected household income standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant, or their claiming tax filer in the case of a tax dependent, is eligible for an exemption if they have a projected household income that does not qualify them as an applicable taxpayer according to 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b) or does not qualify them for cost‑sharing reductions according to 45 CFR 155.305(g)(1)(i)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP provider access standards (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federally-facilitated Exchange or a State on the Federally-facilitated Exchanges with an Effective Provider Access Review Program must ensure that each QHP provides sufficient access to providers in a manner that meets the standards specified in §156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii) for network plans, or §156.236(a) for non-network plans, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges and State-based Exchanges on the Federal Platform must ensure QHPs meet applicable §156.230 or §156.236 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — in-network provider requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective Provider Access Review Program must ensure that a QHP issuer that uses a network ensures that the in-network providers, as available to all enrollees, include essential community providers (ECPs) in accordance with §156.235, and maintains a network sufficient in number and types of providers, including providers specializing in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure that all services will be accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The QHP issuer's provider network must be consistent with the rules for network plans of section 2702(c) of the PHS Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — non-network plan provider requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective Provider Access Review Program must ensure that a QHP issuer that does not use a network (a non-network plan) provides access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and providers specializing in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure services accessible without unreasonable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — State statutory standards and delegation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has established provider access standards set forth in State statute or regulation, consistent with §156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii), and reports to CMS whether the State has delegated authority to some entity other than the State Department of Insurance to perform any or all provider access review activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — reporting systems and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process must include reporting systems for State required provider access metrics and documentation of methodology and the State provides descriptions of all data collection systems, resources, templates, and methodologies used by the State or delegated entity to collect and review provider access data; and the State receives from issuers data and documentation sufficient to conduct the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — compliance procedures and enforcement framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process must include procedures to ensure full and ongoing compliance with State provider access standards and enforcement frameworks applicable to issuers that fail to meet provider access standards so that those issuers come into compliance, including standardized processes to assess issuer efforts to come into compliance and implementing justification and exception processes for issuers that have not yet or cannot meet requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — review timelines and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State establishes and maintains clear procedures and timeline requirements for regular provider access reviews, including processes that ensure reviews occur prior to each plan year's QHP certification cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — consumer complaint monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related provider access complaints to ensure sufficient access to providers consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(B) of the Affordable Care Act and State statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program — non-network plan access monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process to collect and review information capable of demonstrating whether non-network plans provide access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS determination and exceptions for Effective Provider Access Review Program
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will determine whether a State has an Effective Provider Access Review Program based on information demonstrating whether the program meets the criteria; CMS may grant an exception if it determines doing so is in the interests of qualified individuals in the State; CMS will notify the FFE State of its decision in writing and reserves the right to evaluate at any time whether circumstances have changed and assume or transition responsibilities accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: State option to conduct ECP certification reviews conditional on meeting criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States may elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews of issuers' plans with or without a provider network provided the State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity to conduct these reviews by satisfying criteria to be considered to have an Effective Essential Community Provider Review Program under §155.1051.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If States do not satisfy criteria, CMS will continue to perform ECP certification reviews consistent with §156.235 (network) and §156.236 (non-network).

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP access standard for network plans (sufficient number & geographic distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective ECP Review Program must ensure that a QHP issuer with a provider network includes in their provider network a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs, where available, to ensure reasonable and timely access to a broad range of such providers for low-income individuals or individuals residing in Health Professional Shortage Areas within the QHP's service area, in accordance with the Exchange's network adequacy standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP access standard for non-network plans (access and payment in full)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective ECP Review Program must ensure that a non-network plan applying for certification demonstrates it provides reasonable and timely access to ECPs that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full so services will be accessible without unreasonable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP statutory/regulatory requirements and plan compliance (minimums, Indian health, category per county)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective ECP Review Program must have established ECP requirements in State statute/regulation and demonstrate that plans meet: (1) minimum percentage requirements under §156.235(a)(2)(i) for network plans and §156.236(b)(1) for non-network plans; (2) the Indian health care provider requirement under §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(A) and §156.236(b)(3); and (3) the category per county requirements for each of the eight ECP category types under §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(B) for network plans and §156.236(b)(2) for non-network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative ECP requirements — demonstration of equivalent access
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with alternative ECP requirements compared to paragraph (c)(1)-(3) must demonstrate how their requirements would continue to promote a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs to ensure reasonable and timely access and an adequate level of service for low-income enrollees or those in HPSAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors CMS will consider when reviewing State ECP Review Program
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will consider multiple factors in its review including: (1) State's legal authority to review plan compliance; (2) evidence that State requirements are consistent with federal ECP requirements or rationale for alternatives; (3) State's definition of ECP if different; (4) whether State utilizes the Federal ECP List or has a process to identify qualified ECPs for network plans; (5) similar process for non-network plans; (6) description of data collection systems/resources/templates/methodologies; (7) whether State generally collects info from QHP issuers regarding contract offers or offers of payment in full; (8) whether State has delegated authority to other entities; (9) whether State has compliance reviews, follow-up procedures, and enforcement frameworks; and (10) whether State has a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related complaints regarding access to ECPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS notification and reevaluation rights for ECP Review Program
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will notify the FFE State electing to conduct ECP certification reviews in writing whether the State is determined to have an Effective ECP Review Program and can conduct reviews. CMS reserves the right to evaluate at any time whether circumstances have changed such that the State has begun to or ceased to satisfy the criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: External audit standard (State Exchange audits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Exchange must ensure that independent audits of State Exchange financial activities and program activities address specified requirements, unless the State Exchange is satisfying certain programmatic audit requirements for a given benefit year as identified by HHS in sub-regulatory guidance or under the SEIPM process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §155.1200(d) for the list of audit requirements and §155.1200(e) for SEIPM substitution where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM program purpose & scope
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM sets forth requirements of the State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement program through which HHS will measure improper payments of APTC administered by State Exchanges; HHS will use SEIPM results to produce an estimate of improper payments aggregated across State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless specified otherwise, all State Exchanges must submit information on an annual basis necessary to support SEIPM processes; HHS will publish aggregated estimate in the Agency Financial Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM applicability date
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of this subpart are applicable beginning January 1, 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM definitions — key program terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines program-specific terms used throughout SEIPM such as Annual Program Schedule, Administrative Appeal, Corrective action plan (CAP), Difference Resolution, Error, Measurement Year, Reporting Year, Sampled Unit Assessment Package, SEIPM, SEIPM Cycle, and Tax household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors are defined as HHS findings that a State Exchange did not correctly apply requirements of subparts D and E related to eligibility/enrollment, APTC eligibility and amount, redeterminations during a plan year, and re-enrollment redeterminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM information submission — Annual Program Schedule timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will issue an Annual Program Schedule to each State Exchange no later than January 5th of the Measurement Year specifying deadlines for all information submissions required under SEIPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM information submission — program documentation required
rubrics_metrics.description: On an annual basis each State Exchange must submit or make available policy, operational and technical documentation concerning business rules and APTC calculations that pertain to consumer eligibility and enrollment processes as well as information that describes the data system architecture such as entity relationship diagrams and data dictionaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM information submission — universe data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Plan Year being reviewed, State Exchanges must submit a listing of the population of tax households with associated QHP enrollments and APTC payments. For each tax household within the universe, the State Exchange must submit: Exchange assigned policy identifier; tax household grouping identifier; SSN inconsistency indicator; citizenship inconsistency indicator; lawful presence inconsistency indicator; annual income inconsistency indicator; non-employer sponsored MEC inconsistency indicator; employer sponsored MEC inconsistency indicator; incarceration inconsistency indicator; residency inconsistency indicator; number of tax household members; and APTC amount paid over the benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universe is used by HHS to select samples for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM information submission — tax household data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each sampled tax household and in a format specified by HHS, State Exchanges must provide: (i) information pertaining to APTC calculations (monthly enrollment premium amounts, monthly APTC payment amounts, monthly SLCSP premiums, amount attributable to EHBs); (ii) enrollment information (dates/amounts of effectuation payments, premium payment amount, policy start/end dates); (iii) SEP determination information including attestations, documentary evidence, electronic verification info, and timing; (iv) information about timing of QHP certification/approval and decertification/suppression; (v) per-person information used in APTC calculation including attestations, demographic info, evidence of verifications, timing of verifications, manual verification documentation and adjudication timing, good faith extensions, and eligibility redetermination info; and (vi) any consumer submitted documents used to establish eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may supplement with relevant consumer-submitted documents provided by the State Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM sampling procedures — sample size methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each SEIPM cycle HHS will calculate a sample size in aggregate across all State Exchanges. The sample size will be calculated to estimate an improper payment rate, with statistical methodology used, state-specific sample sizes developed taking into consideration overall APTC expenditures, state-level precision goals, and prior improper payment rates; HHS will establish minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity and operational feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM sampling procedures — sample selection and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: On an annual basis HHS will select samples of tax households from the universe data provided by each State Exchange. Following receipt of universe data, HHS will notify each State Exchange of specific records selected for review including total number of sampled tax households, a unique identifier for each sampled tax household, and any specific instructions or requirements needed to facilitate review. HHS will provide this sampled records notification no later than 60 days after receipt of complete universe data from all State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may extend the 60-day timeline for specified reasons (technical issues, data quality issues, other circumstances beyond HHS control). If extension occurs HHS must notify affected State Exchanges in writing with reason and revised notification date and confirm impacts on subsequent timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining payment errors — systematic review and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For each sampled record HHS will conduct a comprehensive systematic review of all information provided by the State Exchange using standardized review criteria, using tax household information submitted under §155.1615(b)(3) supplemented by any relevant consumer-submitted documents gathered by the State Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining payment errors — error identification categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The review will identify whether the State Exchange made any errors related to: (i) enrolling or re-enrolling a consumer into a QHP for which APTC was paid; (ii) consumer eligibility for APTC being paid on the consumer's behalf; (iii) calculating the APTC amount that was paid on the consumer's behalf; and (iv) taking required actions upon changes to a consumer's status that would affect their APTC-related eligibility or payment amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining payment errors — review standards and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will apply consistent review standards based on the APTC-related determination requirements established in subparts D and E of this part, and other applicable provisions of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error evaluation — determining improper payment amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will evaluate each error identified in the review to determine an improper payment amount.
